messages.subject: CV from DSM
parts:
Hello,

I was wondering about the CV reported in the DSM ouput (in this case using the var.gam function). I had seen that this was based on dividing the SE of the estimate by the estimate. I've seen that CV generally is SD/mean, and I'm curious how this differs. Also, is it appropriate to just multiply this number by 100 to get %CV to be directly comparable to the %CV from program DISTANCE?

I also had a question about getting stratum level estimates from a full density raster. For instance, if I predict a DSM to an entire ranch but am curious about pasture level density estimates, and associated variability, what is the best way to go about attaining these estimates? I had assumed the mean density value for all cells within a pasture would correspond to the density for that pasture, but I'm not sure if this is correct, and further don't think this same approach would work for CV. I had also thought to use the full ranch to make the DSM and then just create a prediction grid clipped to the extent of each pasture, thereby attaining a density estimate and variability for each pasture individually.

Any guidance on these issues is much appreciated.

Thanks,

John

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: CV from DSM
parts:
John


Definition of CV: standard deviation is an attribute of a population, standard error is an attribute of a parameter estimate.  We are dealing with the latter when performing abundance estimation.  You are correct that to express CV as a percentage, simply multiply by 100.


Regarding estimation in a sub-region via DSM.  Your second approach (prediction grid consisting of the region of interest) ought to produce both the point estimate as well as a measure of precision of that estimate should work.
